centre.name: Pine Lodge Addiction Recovery

gallery.alt: Brick main building and front ramp of Pine Lodge Addiction Recovery on 8th Avenue in North Central Regina

about_blocks.text: Pine Lodge Addiction Recovery is an inpatient addiction treatment centre at 3535 8th Avenue in North Central Regina. Its main program runs 42 days, and Pine Lodge describes its care as client centred and trauma informed. It is accredited through Accreditation Canada.
about_blocks.html: Pine Lodge Addiction Recovery is an inpatient addiction treatment centre at 3535 8th Avenue in North Central Regina. Its main program runs 42 days, and Pine Lodge describes its care as client centred and trauma informed. It is accredited through Accreditation Canada.

about_blocks.text: Before Regina, Pine Lodge operated in Indian Head until a fire on Christmas Eve 2020 shut it down for close to two years. It moved into a fully renovated building in Regina in October 2022, and the old Pine Lodge sign came along and now stands in the courtyard.
about_blocks.html: Before Regina, Pine Lodge operated in Indian Head until a fire on Christmas Eve 2020 shut it down for close to two years. It moved into a fully renovated building in Regina in October 2022, and the old Pine Lodge sign came along and now stands in the courtyard.

about_blocks.text: Clients come in through a referral package: a referral form and a medical form, usually filled out with a referring counsellor. The form asks for a Saskatchewan health number, and Pine Lodge expects clients to come straight from detox into treatment, since there is no detox on site. Counsellors work with each person on an individual case plan and a relapse prevention plan built around the supports they will have back home.

about_blocks.text: In 2022 Pine Lodge adopted model standards of care based on British Columbia's provincial standards for adult residential substance use services. The centre sits on Treaty 4 territory, says it is committed to the Truth and Reconciliation Commission's calls to action, and has a cultural program counsellor on staff.
about_blocks.html: In 2022 Pine Lodge adopted model standards of care based on British Columbia's provincial standards for adult residential substance use services. The centre sits on Treaty 4 territory, says it is committed to the Truth and Reconciliation Commission's calls to action, and has a cultural program counsellor on staff.

about_blocks.text: After the 42 days, people can move into Pine Lodge's post-treatment program. It is a second-stage program for adults 18 and older who recently finished treatment: half-day counselling groups, one-to-one sessions with post house counsellors, and short-term supportive housing that grew from 11 to 25 beds over the last year. In February 2026 the Saskatchewan Health Authority began funding 16 sober living spaces in two Pine Lodge homes separate from the main building. A vocational support program is still being developed. For referrals, call the intake line at 306-510-1893.

centre.faq_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Pine Lodge Addiction Recovery

faqs.question: How long is treatment at Pine Lodge?

answer_blocks.text: The inpatient program is 42 days. People who finish can then apply to Pine Lodge's post-treatment program, which adds group and one-to-one counselling and short-term supportive housing.
answer_blocks.html: The inpatient program is 42 days. People who finish can then apply to Pine Lodge's post-treatment program, which adds group and one-to-one counselling and short-term supportive housing.

faqs.question: Is Pine Lodge funded by the Saskatchewan Health Authority or private?

answer_blocks.text: Pine Lodge does not publish a client fee, and its beds have had public funding. The province paid for 10 more inpatient beds in 2019, bringing Pine Lodge to 33, and in 2026 the Saskatchewan Health Authority signed an agreement to fund 16 of its sober living spaces at $863,000 a year. In August 2026, MBC News described Pine Lodge as a non-profit charity funded by the Saskatchewan Health Authority, with 38 inpatient beds. Ask the intake line whether any cost applies to you.

faqs.question: How do I get a referral to Pine Lodge?

answer_blocks.text: Download the referral package from the Inpatient Treatment page of the Pine Lodge website. It has a referral form and a medical form, and it is usually completed with an addictions counsellor or other referring worker. Questions go to the intake line at 306-510-1893.

faqs.question: What happens after the 42 day program?

answer_blocks.text: Pine Lodge runs a second-stage post-treatment program. It offers half-day counselling groups, one-to-one sessions with post house counsellors, and short-term supportive housing with recovery support workers. Participants are expected to stay sober, take part in programming and work toward education, a job and housing in their community.

faqs.question: Who can join the post-treatment program?

answer_blocks.text: Adults 18 and older who recently completed an addiction recovery program and need transitional support. Most come from Pine Lodge's own inpatient program, but group and one-to-one sessions are also open as outpatient services. Contact intake@pinelodgerecovery.ca for referral details.

faqs.question: Where is Pine Lodge and how do I get there?

answer_blocks.text: Pine Lodge is at 3535 8th Avenue in North Central Regina. It is about 45 minutes from Moose Jaw and Indian Head, roughly 30 minutes from Lumsden and about two and a half hours from Saskatoon by car.

faqs.question: What is Pine Lodge's approach to treatment?

answer_blocks.text: Care is client centred and trauma informed. Each client builds an individual case plan and a relapse prevention plan with a counsellor, using resources available in their home community, and Pine Lodge follows model standards of care adopted in 2022.
